svg.text: Requirements — WhatsApp (a fan-out chat at planetary scale)
FRs come from "what do I see when I open the app?" · NFRs are quantified · below-the-line items stay below the line
Functional (4 — small on purpose)
FR1 · Start group chats — a group of 2
is exactly a 1:1 chat (one entity)
FR2 · Send + receive messages between users
send once → fan out to EVERY member
FR3 · Media attachments — images, video, audio
uploads can be hundreds of MB
FR4 · Read messages after being offline
the DEVICE was offline, not the person
Out of scope (say it once, then stop):
audio/video calling · presence indicators · spam / contact scraping
Non-functional (quantified + in context)
NFR1 · low latency ≈ 500 ms delivery
100 vs 500 ms is imperceptible — real budget
NFR2 · guaranteed delivery — never lose one
write server-side, ack from client to prove it
NFR3 · high throughput — billions of users (~2B)
~100B+ messages/day; chat server = hot path
NFR4 · data is toxic sludge — don't keep it
E2E-encrypted, ~30-day retention, purge early
NFR5 · fault tolerance — components die always
no single-server failure may take the app down
The numbers that come back later (memorize THEM):
500 ms budget · 30-day purge · 2M connections/server (WhatsApp's number) ⇒ ~1 000 chat servers
100-record DynamoDB transactions ⇒ group chats ≤ 100 · 1B users × 100 msgs/day × 1 KB ≈ 100 TB/day
This is a STATEFUL-CONNECTION + FAN-OUT problem — not a storage problem
· the chat server HOLDS live WebSocket connections → scaling it is the hard part (deep dive 1).
· every message multiplies into N inbox copies → the data model exists to serve that write multiplicity.
